'''Nancy L. Craig''' is a professor emerita of [[molecular biology]] and [[genetics]] at the [[Johns Hopkins University School of Medicine]].<ref name="craig_jhu">{{cite web |title=Nancy Craig, Ph.D. |url=http://www.bs.jhmi.edu/mbg/craiglab/people.html |website=Johns Hopkins University |accessdate=4 September 2018}}</ref> She has done pioneering research on the molecular mechanisms of [[transposable element]]s, or mobile sequences of [[DNA]] found in the [[genome]]s of most known organisms.<ref name="trivedi_2012">{{cite journal |last1=Trivedi |first1=B. P. |title=Profile of Nancy L. Craig |journal=Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences |date=13 August 2012 |volume=109 |issue=36 |pages=14283–14284 |doi=10.1073/pnas.1212357109|pmc=3437901 |pmid=22891344 |bibcode=2012PNAS..10914283T |doi-access=free }}</ref>

==Education==
Craig grew up in Concord, Calif., graduated from Concord High School and attended [[Bryn Mawr College]], a [[women's college]], as an undergraduate. She later described the environment as "empowering" due to lack of female role models elsewhere in science.<ref name=trivedi_2012 /> After graduating in 1973 summa cum laude with an A.B. in biology and chemistry, Craig attended graduate school at [[Cornell University]], where she studied the chemistry of [[DNA repair]] and the mechanisms of the cellular [[SOS response]] to [[DNA damage]]. She was particularly intrigued by the life cycle of the [[lambda phage]], a [[virus]] that infects [[bacteria]] and is capable of integrating its [[genome]] into that of the host cell. Craig received her Ph.D. in 1980 and then joined the laboratory of [[Howard Nash]] at the [[National Institutes of Health]] as a [[postdoctoral fellow]], where she continued to study lambda phage genome integration.<ref name=trivedi_2012 /><ref name=craig_jhu />

==Academic career==
Craig joined the faculty in the departments of Microbiology & Immunology and Biochemistry & Biophysics at the [[University of California, San Francisco]] in 1984.<ref name=craig_jhu /> She focused her research group's early work on developing ''[[in vitro]]'' systems for studying the [[transposon]] [[Tn7]] and later cited the success of this effort as one of her career highlights.<ref name="nybo_2014">{{cite journal |last1=Nybo |first1=Kristie |title=Profile of Nancy Craig |journal=BioTechniques |date=1 January 2014 |volume=56 |issue=1 |page=11 |doi=10.2144/000114120|doi-access=free }}</ref> In 1992, Craig moved her laboratory from UCSF to [[Johns Hopkins University]], where she remains a professor emerita.<ref name=trivedi_2012 /> Craig was a [[Howard Hughes Medical Institute]] Investigator from 1991 to 2015.<ref name="hhmi">{{cite web |title=Nancy L. Craig, Ph.D. |url=https://www.hhmi.org/scientists/nancy-l-craig |website=Howard Hughes Medical Institute |accessdate=4 September 2018}}</ref> She was elected to the [[National Academy of Sciences]] in 2010.<ref name="nas">{{cite web |title=Nancy Craig |url=https://www.nasonline.org/directory-entry/nancy-l-craig-pv835v/ |website=National Academy of Sciences |access-date=4 September 2018}}</ref>

==Research interests==
Throughout her career, Craig has focused her research on [[transposable element]]s, or sequences of [[DNA]] that can change position in a [[genome]]. Transposons are found in the genomes of nearly all known organisms and gave rise to a large fraction of the [[human genome]].<ref name=trivedi_2012 /> In addition to the unusually specific [[transposon]] [[Tn7]], her research has focused on families of transposons known as [[hAT transposon]]s and [[piggyBac]].<ref name=trivedi_2012 /><ref name="craig_research">{{cite web |title=Craig Lab Research |url=http://www.bs.jhmi.edu/mbg/craiglab/research.html |website=Johns Hopkins University |accessdate=4 September 2018}}</ref> 

Since 2021, Craig has been senior vice president of Genetic Engineering and Mobile Elements and chair of the Scientific Advisory Board at SalioGen Therapeutics, a Lexington, Mass., corporation developing new methods of genetic medicine.<ref name=“saliogen”>{{cite web | title=SalioGen Therapeutics Strengthens Management with Key Additions to Leadership Team to Advance Its Gene Coding Platform | date=28 July 2021 | url=https://finance.yahoo.com/news/saliogen-therapeutics-strengthens-management-key-120000628.html |accessdate=8 February 2024}}</ref>
